instructions: At least 1 hour ahead: rinse the moong dal and put it in a bowl with 1 cup of water. Let it soak for 1 hour, or up to 4. It will swell and turn tender but still crunchy.
Drain the dal well. Chop the cucumber into small pieces and grate the carrot. Remove the seeds from the green chili and chop it fine. Chop 2 tbsp of cilantro.
Put the dal, cucumber, carrot, coconut and cilantro in a large bowl.
Heat the coconut oil in a small pan over medium heat. Add the mustard seeds and wait for them to pop, about 30 seconds.
Add the asafoetida, green chili and curry leaves. Stir for 20 seconds until the curry leaves crisp, then take the pan off the heat.
Pour the tempering over the salad and toss.
Just before eating, squeeze in the juice of the lemon and add the salt. Toss and serve in bowls.
To pack it for lunch, keep the salad and the tempering together in a container in the fridge for up to 1 day, and add the lemon and salt when you're ready to eat.
advance_prep_notes: soak the moong dal at least 1 hour ahead
method_notes: Kosambari has no source with an average rating and 20 or more ratings: Archana's Kitchen shows 17,316 ratings but no average, and the other pages had 0 to 11 votes. It leads with Archana's Kitchen for the soaked dal, cucumber, coconut and mustard tempering, with 1 hour of soaking from Vidhya's Home Cooking (Archana soaks 4 hours). The carrot comes from Rachna Cooks and Vidhya's, as the list promises. Lemon and salt go in at the end because Vidhya's and Smitha Kalluraya both say they make the salad watery if added early.
